reasoning_traces.think:
Localized Conformal Prediction (LCP) addresses the marginal coverage issue in standard conformal prediction by introducing a similarity-based weighting scheme. It defines a localizer function H(x, x') that assigns higher weights to calibration points closer to the test point x. This leads to tighter intervals where predictions are more confident, while preserving finite-sample validity. The core equation w_i(x) ∝ H(x, X_i) encodes how each calibration point contributes to the prediction interval. When applied to GSE’s game features such as weather bucket, QB tier, and rest differential, LCP enables dynamic adjustment of uncertainty bounds tailored to specific match contexts. The method supports both fixed kernels (e.g., Gaussian) and learned ones from residual-QRFs, allowing for adaptive localization. Sample splitting mitigates computational overhead by precomputing weights on a held-out set. Theoretical guarantees ensure marginal coverage remains valid even under conditional variability, making LCP suitable for high-stakes forecasting environments like sports intelligence.
